headline: Learned representations of proteins and ligands drive binding and design prediction
label: Learned Molecular Representations
summary: Recent items pair structure-aware encoders with diffusion and reinforcement learning to enforce physical validity and multi-objective design criteria.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations of proteins, small molecules, RNA, and peptides, paired with graph, point-cloud, or sequence encoders to predict binding and properties. Several items fuse modalities or extend generative models: UACD-ACPs couples a ProtBERT and physicochemical fusion classifier with a conditional diffusion generator, and AI-MedCraft applies Pareto-guided reinforcement learning to multi-objective small-molecule design. DiffDock-Pocket is fine-tuned with reinforcement learning on non-differentiable physical validity, and SSP decouples structural objectives in protein inverse folding through separate preference models. The energy-guided denoising framework pretrains 3D molecular encoders with a chemistry-aware noise generator. What is new is the use of reinforcement learning and preference optimization to impose physical validity and multiple structural objectives on generative models. Reported results are benchmark-specific, and the items do not establish generalization beyond them.
